items.title: Hark Pro: What It Is, Features, Pricing and How to Use It
items.content:
Hark Pro is the proactive AI assistant from Hark, the company founded by Brett Adcock. It launched free on web, iOS and Android on 6 October 2026, and instead of waiting for you to ask, it reads your inbox and calendar and suggests what it can take off your plate. I tested it on launch day in the video below. This guide covers what Hark Pro is, its features and plans, and how to get started.

Key takeaways

- Hark Pro launched 6 October 2026 on web, iOS and Android.

- It’s free, with $20 and $100 monthly tiers for more usage.

- Its Handoff feature completes tasks on a dedicated cloud computer.

- Hark plans to release hardware in 2027.

## What Hark Pro is

Hark calls Hark Pro “an operating system for your life”. Connect your email and calendar, and it learns your routines — then proactively suggests actions, like booking a table, paying a bill, or noticing a flight with no hotel booked. It’s built by Hark, the AI company Brett Adcock started after founding Figure AI and Archer Aviation.

## Hark Pro features

- Proactive inbox — reads your email and suggests action items you approve with a tap.

- Handoff — for each task, it spins up a dedicated cloud computer with its own browser, files and terminal, logs into the accounts it needs, and does the clicking for you while you watch.

- Panels — mini-apps you create by describing them: workouts, productivity, packages, calendar.

- Projects — long-running threads with their own files for big tasks.

- Scheduled tasks and “prep my day” briefings.

- Integrations — Gmail, Slack, GitHub, LinkedIn, Notion, Amazon, PayPal and more.

## How to get started with Hark Pro

- Sign up on the web or download the iOS or Android app.

- Connect your email — Hark recommends it first.

- Answer its opening question: what’s one thing it could take off your plate this week?

- Try “prep my day”, then create a panel for something you track.

My full launch-day walkthrough is in my Hark AI agent guide.

## What Hark Pro can’t do yet

- No phone calls yet — Adcock has said they’ll get there.

- Voice is input only; it doesn’t talk back.

- Some tasks are slower than doing them yourself, according to early testers.

## Hark Pro and your privacy

Handoff logs into your accounts on a cloud computer, so you’re trusting Hark with real access. Read its privacy policy, connect accounts gradually, and approve payments yourself.

## Hark Pro Handoff explained

Handoff is the engine behind Hark Pro’s tasks. When you ask it to do something on the web — book a restaurant, order groceries, renew something — Hark starts a dedicated virtual computer in the cloud for that task, with its own browser, file system and terminal. It signs in to the accounts it needs and clicks, types and scrolls like a person would, and you can watch it work in a small window.

That design has two benefits: it can use almost any website, not just ones with an official integration, and you can see exactly what it’s doing. The trade-off is speed — a real browser session takes time.

## Hark Pro tips from my testing

- Start with email only — it’s where most of the proactive suggestions come from.

- Use “prep my day” every morning — it’s the most useful habit-forming feature.

- Build one panel for something you check daily, like packages or workouts.

- Use Projects for anything that spans days, like planning a trip.

- Say stop if it starts something you didn’t mean — it listens.

- Approve payments yourself until you trust it.

## Hark Pro vs the Hark hardware

Hark has said its first devices arrive in 2027, and that Hark Pro will get better with dedicated AI hardware. For now, Hark Pro is the software layer — and it already works on the phone and laptop you have. Learning it now means you’re ready when the hardware lands.

It’s strongest for personal admin — the small, repetitive tasks that eat your week.

## Should you try Hark Pro?

Yes — it’s free, it takes minutes to set up, and the proactive approach is genuinely different. For my verdict, see my Hark Pro review. Try Hark Pro on one real task this week and see what it saves you.

If you already use another AI assistant, you don’t have to switch completely. I keep Hark Pro for personal admin, where its proactive suggestions shine, and use other agents for business work. Running two assistants side by side is the easiest way to learn which one fits each job, and it costs nothing while Hark’s free plan covers your usage.

A final practical note: Hark Pro is changing fast. Features like phone calls and faster task handling are clearly on the roadmap, and the hardware launch in 2027 will reshape how it works. If you try it now and it doesn’t fit, check back in a few months. The free plan means there’s nothing to lose by keeping your account and testing each update as it rolls out.

items.content_html:
Hark Pro is the proactive AI assistant from Hark, the company founded by Brett Adcock. It launched free on web, iOS and Android on 6 October 2026, and instead of waiting for you to ask, it reads your inbox and calendar and suggests what it can take off your plate. I tested it on launch day in the video below. This guide covers what Hark Pro is, its features and plans, and how to get started.

Key takeaways

  • Hark Pro launched 6 October 2026 on web, iOS and Android.
  • It’s free, with $20 and $100 monthly tiers for more usage.
  • Its Handoff feature completes tasks on a dedicated cloud computer.
  • Hark plans to release hardware in 2027.

What Hark Pro is

Hark calls Hark Pro “an operating system for your life”. Connect your email and calendar, and it learns your routines — then proactively suggests actions, like booking a table, paying a bill, or noticing a flight with no hotel booked. It’s built by Hark, the AI company Brett Adcock started after founding Figure AI and Archer Aviation.

Hark Pro features

  • Proactive inbox — reads your email and suggests action items you approve with a tap.
  • Handoff — for each task, it spins up a dedicated cloud computer with its own browser, files and terminal, logs into the accounts it needs, and does the clicking for you while you watch.
  • Panels — mini-apps you create by describing them: workouts, productivity, packages, calendar.
  • Projects — long-running threads with their own files for big tasks.
  • Scheduled tasks and “prep my day” briefings.
  • Integrations — Gmail, Slack, GitHub, LinkedIn, Notion, Amazon, PayPal and more.

How to get started with Hark Pro

  • Sign up on the web or download the iOS or Android app.
  • Connect your email — Hark recommends it first.
  • Answer its opening question: what’s one thing it could take off your plate this week?
  • Try “prep my day”, then create a panel for something you track.

My full launch-day walkthrough is in my Hark AI agent guide.

What Hark Pro can’t do yet

  • No phone calls yet — Adcock has said they’ll get there.
  • Voice is input only; it doesn’t talk back.
  • Some tasks are slower than doing them yourself, according to early testers.

Hark Pro and your privacy

Handoff logs into your accounts on a cloud computer, so you’re trusting Hark with real access. Read its privacy policy, connect accounts gradually, and approve payments yourself.

Hark Pro Handoff explained

Handoff is the engine behind Hark Pro’s tasks. When you ask it to do something on the web — book a restaurant, order groceries, renew something — Hark starts a dedicated virtual computer in the cloud for that task, with its own browser, file system and terminal. It signs in to the accounts it needs and clicks, types and scrolls like a person would, and you can watch it work in a small window.

That design has two benefits: it can use almost any website, not just ones with an official integration, and you can see exactly what it’s doing. The trade-off is speed — a real browser session takes time.

Hark Pro tips from my testing

  • Start with email only — it’s where most of the proactive suggestions come from.
  • Use “prep my day” every morning — it’s the most useful habit-forming feature.
  • Build one panel for something you check daily, like packages or workouts.
  • Use Projects for anything that spans days, like planning a trip.
  • Say stop if it starts something you didn’t mean — it listens.
  • Approve payments yourself until you trust it.

Hark Pro vs the Hark hardware

Hark has said its first devices arrive in 2027, and that Hark Pro will get better with dedicated AI hardware. For now, Hark Pro is the software layer — and it already works on the phone and laptop you have. Learning it now means you’re ready when the hardware lands.

Daily planning

“Prep my day” checks calendar and inbox

Tracking

Panels for workouts, packages, productivity and more

It’s strongest for personal admin — the small, repetitive tasks that eat your week.

Should you try Hark Pro?

Yes — it’s free, it takes minutes to set up, and the proactive approach is genuinely different. For my verdict, see my Hark Pro review. Try Hark Pro on one real task this week and see what it saves you.

If you already use another AI assistant, you don’t have to switch completely. I keep Hark Pro for personal admin, where its proactive suggestions shine, and use other agents for business work. Running two assistants side by side is the easiest way to learn which one fits each job, and it costs nothing while Hark’s free plan covers your usage.

A final practical note: Hark Pro is changing fast. Features like phone calls and faster task handling are clearly on the roadmap, and the hardware launch in 2027 will reshape how it works. If you try it now and it doesn’t fit, check back in a few months. The free plan means there’s nothing to lose by keeping your account and testing each update as it rolls out.

items.title: Hark Pro Review: Is the Proactive AI Assistant Worth It?
items.content:
This Hark Pro review is based on my own launch-day testing plus early reports from other testers. Short version: Hark Pro has the best onboarding and design of any AI assistant I’ve used, and it’s genuinely proactive — but it can be slow, it can’t make calls yet, and it needs deep access to your accounts. Watch my test below, then here’s the full verdict.

Key takeaways

- Overall: 7.6/10 — brilliant design and onboarding, still early.

- Best for personal admin: inbox, bookings, bills, daily planning.

- Weak spots: speed, no phone calls, privacy detail.

- It’s free to try — paid tiers only add usage.

## Hark Pro review: the verdict

Hark Pro is the most polished AI assistant I’ve tested. Signing up, connecting email and getting useful suggestions took minutes. When I asked it to book an Italian restaurant, it asked the right follow-up questions and started booking one of my actual favourites. It feels like the Apple of AI agents.

But it’s version one. Some tasks take longer than doing them yourself, it can’t make phone calls yet, and you’re trusting it with real access to your accounts. Great foundations; not finished.

## What other testers found

Early hands-on reports back this up. A Fast Company beta test found Hark spotted an oil change in the reporter’s email and handled much of the booking, though he still had to give some details and pick a time. A Gizmodo test found its food ordering slower than doing it manually. Hark’s own design lead has said it might not be the fastest assistant, but it aims for a better result.

## How I tested Hark Pro

I signed up on the free plan on launch day, connected my email, and gave it real tasks: booking a restaurant for two on a specific evening, building a productivity panel, setting up a project, and running “prep my day”. I also explored the integrations list, scheduled tasks and voice input. I didn’t connect payment accounts, and I stopped the restaurant booking before it completed.

That’s a first-week test, not months of use — so I’ve combined it with what other early testers reported.

## Hark Pro review: what impressed me most

Two things. First, the onboarding: connect email, answer one question, and it’s already useful. Second, the proactivity. “Prep my day” checked my calendar and inbox, told me my inbox was clean, and offered to pull in sales numbers before a 4pm meeting. That’s what a real assistant does.

The panels are clever too — describing a mini-app in plain English and getting a working dashboard is the kind of thing that makes non-technical people fall in love with AI.

## Hark Pro review: what needs work

Speed is the big one. Because Handoff drives a real browser on a cloud computer, some tasks take longer than doing them yourself. Phone calls aren’t supported, and voice is input only. And while Hark talks about privacy, there’s little independent detail yet on how it handles your data — which matters when it’s logging into your accounts.

## Hark Pro review: final thoughts on value

For a free product, Hark Pro delivers a lot: a genuinely proactive assistant, clean design and useful panels. Most people won’t need a paid tier, since paying only raises your usage limits. The question isn’t really price — it’s whether you’re comfortable giving an assistant this much access, and whether its speed suits the tasks you have.

If you’re a busy professional drowning in small admin tasks, it’s worth a week of testing. If you’re building business automations, a customisable agent like Hermes will serve you better.

## Who should use Hark Pro

Use it if you want a personal assistant for email, bookings, bills and planning, and you’re comfortable connecting your accounts. Skip it for now if speed is critical, you need phone calls, or you can’t share account access. My final Hark Pro review score: 7.6/10, and one to watch as the 2027 hardware arrives.

I’ll update this review as Hark ships improvements, especially on speed, phone calls and privacy detail, which are the three areas holding back a higher score today. If those land, Hark Pro could become the default personal assistant for a lot of people, and the 2027 hardware could make it even more useful away from a screen.

## Best Chinese AI app reviews

### 1. DeepSeek — the best Chinese AI app for most people

DeepSeek is the one I use most. The chat app is free on the web, iOS and Android, it’s excellent in English, and its models are open weight, so developers can run them too. What makes it stand out right now is DeepSeek Harness — a free, open-source agent harness that now has a desktop app for Mac and Windows, with plugins, scheduled automation and agent teams. I covered it in my DeepSeek Harness desktop guide.

### 2. Qwen — best for open-weight models

Alibaba’s Qwen app is the second-biggest AI app in China, and the Qwen models are some of the most popular open-weight models in the world, available in sizes from tiny to huge. If you run local AI, you’ve almost certainly used a Qwen model.

### 3. Doubao — the most-used AI app in China

ByteDance’s Doubao is the clear leader by users inside China, with roughly 2.3 times the monthly users of its nearest rival. It’s built mainly for the Chinese market, so for English speakers DeepSeek or Qwen are usually the better pick.

### 4. Kimi — best for long documents and coding

Moonshot AI’s Kimi is known for long-context work and strong coding models, and it ranks highly on public model leaderboards. Its newest models are also available through OpenRouter, so you can plug them into agents like Hermes.

### 5. MiniMax — best for models plus media

MiniMax builds language models alongside voice, image and video generation. I’ve used MiniMax M3 inside Hermes through Ollama for real generation tasks, and its speech models for voice agents.

### 6. Yuanbao — best inside WeChat

Tencent’s Yuanbao brings AI into the WeChat world. It uses DeepSeek alongside Tencent’s own models, and much of its usage happens inside WeChat rather than the standalone app.

### 7. Kling — best for AI video

Kuaishou’s Kling is one of the best-known AI video generators. If you make content, it’s the Chinese AI app worth testing for text-to-video and image-to-video.

### 8. Quark — best for AI search

Alibaba’s Quark combines search, browsing and AI answers, and it’s one of the most-used AI products in China by some rankings.

### 9. GLM / Z.ai — best for coding agents

Zhipu AI’s GLM models are popular open-weight options for coding and agent work, and they’re widely available through providers that plug into agent harnesses.

### 10. ERNIE — Baidu’s assistant

Baidu’s ERNIE models power its assistant and search features. It’s most useful if you work in the Chinese market and the Baidu ecosystem.

They’re widely used and genuinely good, but be sensible. Chinese AI companies operate under Chinese law, so I don’t put private client data or anything sensitive into their hosted apps. Read each app’s privacy policy, avoid sharing personal or confidential information, and use them for research, drafting and testing.
